title: Common-stage Verdier data and realization predicates
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$. Use the coefficient categories, derived tensor and internal Hom, and constructible exceptional functors of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. A common-stage duality consists of finite rational Verdier data of [def-sf-rational-verdier-data], coherent scalar comparisons, one exact common-stage anti-equivalence with its biduality, a specified $\Omega$-linear category structure, a dualizing object and finite-origin comparisons and evaluation. Its equations fix the coefficient action, object formulas, identity comparison components, scalar squares, evaluation and actual biduality descent, naturality, and the forward and inverse biduality and evaluation formulas on every split retract. For such a duality $B$, an internal-Hom identification supplies permitted pairs, identifies its dual with the actual common-stage internal Hom into $B.\omega$, and requires bijectivity of the transpose of its specified evaluation. The dualizing predicate means that $B.\omega$ is the exceptional image of the actual coefficient unit at $a_X$, and that each finite origin has the dualizing identification of [def-sf-rational-verdier-identifications] for that same exceptional system. These define data and a predicate, without an existence assertion.
